title: Build Secrets and SSH Mounts knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Build Secrets and SSH Mounts”?
options: Print credentials to logs to confirm configuration.
Use a controlled secret mechanism and restrict credentials to the service or build step that needs them.
Copy secrets into the final image so the runtime can read them.
Place passwords in ordinary Dockerfile ARG and assume they vanish after the build.
questions.answer_key: Use a controlled secret mechanism and restrict credentials to the service or build step that needs them.
questions.explanation: Docker’s build-secret guidance recommends secret/SSH mounts instead of ordinary build args or environment variables for build-time secrets.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering build secrets and ssh mounts, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to build secrets and ssh mounts fails, which response is best?
options: Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For build secrets and ssh mounts, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
